one_liner: Hand-written SQL scanner/parser inside CrossDB's embedded RDBMS, claimed 10x faster than Flex/Bison-generated code.
what_it_does: CrossDB is an embedded/server OLTP relational database written in C. Instead of generating its SQL front end with Flex/Bison, it hand-writes a character-table-driven scanner (src/parser/xdb_token.c) and a recursive-descent parser (src/parser/xdb_parser.c) that are compiled together as one translation unit. The parser is not a standalone library: it converts SQL text into CrossDB's internal statement structs and is only reachable through CrossDB's own connection/exec API, not as a reusable grammar for other projects.
how_it_is_fast: A hand-written recursive-descent parser calls a hand-written scanner directly, skipping the generated DFA table-walk that Flex output uses; the scanner classifies characters with a 256-entry static lookup table (s_tok_type) and switches on token type inline. Because xdb_token.c is textually #included into xdb_parser.c, the compiler can inline across the scanner/parser boundary in a way two separately compiled Flex/Bison translation units cannot. The ~10x and ~1/3-code-size figures come from a single unsourced FAQ bullet with no published benchmark script, hardware, or compiler flags.
when_to_use: Embedding a small in-memory/on-disk OLTP relational engine in C/C++/Go/Python/Rust and wanting its internal SQL parsing fast without adding Flex/Bison to the build
High-frequency, short OLTP-style SQL statements parsed repeatedly rather than parsed once and cached
Needing portability across Linux/macOS/Windows/FreeBSD and x86/ARM/PowerPC/MIPS without a Flex/Bison toolchain dependency
Wanting a reentrant, thread-safe SQL front end with no shared global parser state across connections
Accepting CrossDB's own MySQL-flavored SQL dialect rather than needing a general-purpose or standard SQL grammar
when_not_to_use: You need a standalone, reusable SQL lexer/parser library: CrossDB's scanner and parser are internal to the engine and not exposed as an independent API
You need the 10x claim substantiated: no benchmark script, workload, hardware, or scanner-only vs parser-only breakdown is published
You need a mature, standard SQL dialect: the project itself says it is 'still in its early stages and currently lacks stability'
You need active upstream development: last commit 2025-06-20, 268 stars, 21 forks, and only 3 open issues suggest limited real-world usage exercising parser edge cases
Your dataset won't fit in available memory or lives on network-mounted disks, which the project's own FAQ lists as limitations of the engine the parser serves

integration.dependencies: none (single C source tree; optional Go/Python bindings and JNI wrapper ship separately in the repo)
integration.min_toolchain: not documented precisely; uses _GNU_SOURCE, stdint.h/stdbool.h; built with GCC via Makefile/CMake, MinGW64 for Windows
integration.platforms: Linux/macOS/FreeBSD/Windows; x86 32/64-bit, ARM, PowerPC, MIPS per README
integration.thread_safety: FAQ states the scanner/parser is 'fully reentrant and thread-safe'; not independently verified beyond reading the source
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it replaces Flex/Bison output inside CrossDB itself, but only as part of the whole engine; it cannot be swapped into another project's own grammar

gotchas: Scanner and parser aren't separable: xdb_token.c is #included directly into xdb_parser.c, so the tokenizer can't be linked or used on its own
Parsing is tied to CrossDB's own metadata structs (xdb_stmt_t, xdb_tblm_t, xdb_tblm lookups) — output is not a generic, reusable AST
Functions use XDB_STATIC internal linkage and file-scope static tables, confirming this is compiled as one amalgamated unit rather than a modular library
One closed GitHub issue documents a parser bug on inequality expressions (Aug 2024), fixed before the 2025-06-20 last commit but indicative of a young grammar
pick_this_over_siblings_when: All the catalogued siblings (logos, LRSTAR, simd-lexing, lexer-exp, Gigatoken, Accelerated-Zig-Parser, StreamTok, Ragel) are extractable, general-purpose lexers/tokenizers you drop into your own project; CrossDB's parser is only worth it if you're embedding the CrossDB RDBMS itself and want its SQL front end's speed as a side effect, not as a standalone lexer replacement.
verified_claims_summary: CrossDB's docs FAQ claims its hand-written scanner+parser is 'over 10 times faster than Flex/Bison parser tools' and about one-third the code size, stated as a single unsourced bullet in docs/faq.md with no linked benchmark script, hardware, or compiler/flags, and it bundles scanning and parsing together rather than isolating lexer-only throughput.
status_note: Stale by this catalog's threshold (last commit 2025-06-20) with only 268 stars/21 forks, and the project's own README/CONTRIBUTING call it early-stage and not yet stable; MPL-2.0 and copyable as source, but not a drop-in component outside the full CrossDB engine.
